<output>
jp2a
====

jp2a is a simple JPEG to ASCII converter.

The source is available at <https://github.com/cslarsen/jp2a>. This project
used to be hosted on SourceForge.

License
-------

Copyright 2006-2016 Christian Stigen Larsen  
Distributed under the GNU General Public License v2.

You can read the full license in the file COPYING. jp2a also uses other
libraries. These licenses can be found in the file LICENSES.

Usage
-----

jp2a converts JPEG images to ASCII characters. You can specify a mixture of 
files and URLs.

**Basic usage:**

```
jp2a [options] [filename(s) | URL(s)]
```

**Common options:**

- `-` - Read JPEG image from standard input
- `--size=WIDTHxHEIGHT` - Set output dimensions
- `--width=N` - Set output width (height calculated automatically)
- `--height=N` - Set output height (width calculated automatically)
- `--chars=...` - Use specific characters for output (default: "   ...',;:clodxkO0KXNWM")
- `--invert` or `-i` - Invert output image
- `--background=light` or `--background=dark` - Set background type
- `--border` or `-b` - Frame output in a border
- `--colors` - Use ANSI color for text output and CSS color for HTML output
- `--html` - Output in XHTML 1.0 format
- `--output=FILE` - Write output to file
- `--term-fit` or `-f` - Fit image to terminal display
- `--flipx` or `-x` - Flip output horizontally
- `--flipy` or `-y` - Flip output vertically
- `--help` or `-h` - Display help
- `--version` or `-V` - Print version

Examples
--------

Convert and print a JPEG file:

```
jp2a imagefile.jpg
```

Convert with specific dimensions:

```
jp2a --size=40x20 imagefile.jpg
```

Download an image from the web and convert:

```
jp2a http://example.com/image.jpg
```

Use specific characters for output:

```
jp2a --chars=" ...ooxx@@" picture.jpg
```

Read from standard input:

```
cat image.jpg | jp2a --width=76 -
```

Use with ImageMagick to convert other image formats:

```
convert somefile.png jpg:- | jp2a - --width=80
```

Output to HTML:

```
jp2a --html --output=output.html image.jpg
```

For more detailed information, see the man page: `man jp2a`
=== MAN ===
.TH jp2a 1  "September 4, 2006" "version 1.0" "USER COMMANDS"
.SH NAME
jp2a \- convert JPEG images to ASCII
.SH SYNOPSIS
.B jp2a
[
.I options
] [
.I filename(s) | URL(s)
]
.LP
.SH DESCRIPTION
.B jp2a
will convert JPEG images to ASCII characters.  You can specify a mixture of files and URLs.
.SH OPTIONS
.TP
.BI \-
Read JPEG image from standard input
.TP
.B \-\-background=light \-\-background=dark
If you don't want to mess with \-\-invert all the time, just use these instead.
If you are using white characters on a black display, then use --background=dark,
and vice versa.
.TP
.B \-b \-\-border
Frame output image in a border
.TP
.BI \-\-chars= ...
Use the given characters when producing the output ASCII image.  Default is "   ...',;:clodxkO0KXNWM".
.TP
.BI \-\-colors
Use ANSI color for text output and CSS color for HTML output.
.TP
.B \-d \-\-debug
Print debugging information when using libcurl to download images from the net.
.TP
.B \-f \-\-term\-fit
Use the largest dimension that makes the image fit in your terminal display.
.TP
.B \-\-term\-height
Use terminal display height and calculate width based on image aspect ratio.
.TP
.B \-\-term\-width
Use terminal display width and calculate height based on image aspect ratio.
.TP
.B \-z \-\-term\-zoom
Use terminal display width and height.
.TP
.B \-\-fill
When used with \-\-html and \-\-color, then color each output character's background color.  For instance,
if you want to use fill-output on a light background, do

jp2a --color --html --html-fill --background=light somefile.jpg --output=dark.html

To do the same on a light background:

jp2a --color --html --html-fill --background=dark somefile.jpg --output=light.html

The default is to have fill disabled.
.TP
.B \-x \-\-flipx
Flip output image horizontally
.TP
.B \-y \-\-flipy
Flip output image vertically
.TP
.BI \-\-height= N
Set output height.  If only --height is specified, then output width will
be calculated according to the source images aspect ratio.
.TP
.B \-h \-\-help
Display a short help text
.TP
.B \-\-grayscale
Converts image to grayscale when using \-\-html or \-\-colors.
.TP
.B \-\-html
Make ASCII output in strict XHTML 1.0, suitable for viewing with web browsers.
This is useful with big output dimensions, and you want to check the result with a browser with small font.
.TP
.B \-\-html\-fill
Same as \-\-fill.  You should use that option instead.
.TP
.B \-\-html\-no\-bold
Do not use bold text for HTML output.
.TP
.B \-\-html\-raw
Output only the image in HTML codes, leaving out the rest of the webpage, so you can construct
your own.
.TP
.BI \-\-html\-fontsize= N
Set fontsize when using \-\-html output.  Default is 4.
.TP
.BI \-\-html\-title= ...
Set HTML output title.
.TP
.BI \-\-output=...
Write ASCII output to given filename.  To explicitly specify standard output, use \-\-output=\-.
.TP
.B \-i \-\-invert
Invert output image.  If you view a picture with white background, but you are using
a display with light characters on a dark background, you shoudl invert the image.
.TP
.BI \-\-red= ...
.TP
.BI \-\-green= ...
.TP
.BI \-\-blue= ...
When converting from RGB to grayscale, use the given weights to calculate luminance.
These three floating point values must add up to exactly 1.0.
The default is red=0.2989, green=0.5866 and blue=0.1145.
.TP
.BI \-\-size= WIDTHxHEIGHT
Set output dimension.
.TP
.B \-v \-\-verbose
Print some verbose information to standard error when reading each JPEG image.
.TP
.BI \-\-width= N
Set output width.  If you only specify the width, the height will be
calculated automatically.
.TP
.B \-V \-\-version
Print program version.
.TP
.B \-\-zoom
Sets output dimensions to your entire terminal window, disregarding source image
aspect ratio.
.SH RETURN VALUES
jp2a returns 1 when errors are encountered, zero for no errors.
.SH EXAMPLES
Convert and print imagefile.jpg using ASCII characters in 40 columns and 20 rows:
.PP
.B jp2a
\-\-size=40x20 imagefile.jpg
.PP
Download an image off the net, convert and print:
.PP
.B jp2a
http://www.google.com/intl/en/logos/easter_logo.jpg
.PP
Output picture.jpg and picture2.jpg, each 80x25 characters, using the characters " ...ooxx@@" for output:
.PP
.B jp2a
\-\-size=80x25 --chars=" ...ooxx@@" picture.jpg picture2.jpg
.PP
Output image.jpg using 76 columns, height is automatically calculated from aspect ratio of image.jpg
.PP
cat image.jpg |
.B jp2a
\-\-width=76 \-
.PP
If you use jp2a together with ImageMagick's convert(1) then you can make good use of pipes,
and have ImageMagick do all sorts of image conversions and effects on the source image.  For example:
.PP
.B convert
somefile.png jpg:\- |
.B jp2a
\- \-\-width=80
.PP
Check out convert(1) options to see what you can do.  Convert can handle almost any image format,
so with this combination you can convert images in e.g. PDF or AVI files to ASCII.
.PP
Although the default build of jp2a includes automatic downloading of files specified by URLs,
you can explicitly download them by using curl(1) or wget(1), for example:
.PP
.B curl
\-s
http://foo.bar/image.jpg |
.B convert
\- jpg:- |
.B jp2a
\-
.SH DOWNLOADING IMAGES FROM THE NET
If you have compiled jp2a with libcurl(3), you can download images by specifying URLs:

.B jp2a
https://user:pass@foo.com/bar.jpg

The protocols recognized are ftp, ftps, file, http, https and tftp.

If you need more control of the downloading, you should use curl(1) or wget(1) and jp2a
read the image from standard input.

jp2a uses pipe and fork to download images using libcurl (i.e., no exec or system calls) 
and therefore does not worry about malevolently formatted URLs.
.SH GRAYSCALE CONVERSION
You can extract the red channel by doing this:

.B jp2a
somefile.jpg --red=1.0 --green=0.0 --blue=0.0

This will calculate luminance based on Y = R*1.0 + G*0.0 + B*0.0.  The default
values is to use Y = R*0.2989 + G*0.5866 + B*0.1145.
.SH PROJECT HOMEPAGE
The latest version of jp2a and news is always available from https://github.com/cslarsen/jp2a
.SH SEE ALSO
cjpeg(1), djpeg(1), jpegtran(1), convert(1)
.SH BUGS
jp2a does not interpolate when resizing.  If you want better quality, try using convert(1)
and convert the source image to the exact output dimensions before using jp2a.
.PP
Another issue is that jp2a skips some X-pixels along each scanline.  This gives a less
precise output image, and will probably be corrected in future versions.

{"command": "mkdir -p /tmp/tools && cat > /tmp/tools/jenc.py <<'PYEOF'
"""Minimal baseline JPEG encoder (gray or YCbCr), flat quant tables, 8-bit fixed Huffman."""
ZIG = [
 0, 1, 8,16, 9, 2, 3,10,
17,24,32,25,18,11, 4, 5,
12,19,26,33,40,48,41,34,
27,20,13, 6, 7,14,21,28,
35,42,49,56,57,50,43,36,
29,22,15,23,30,37,44,51,
58,59,52,45,38,31,39,46,
53,60,61,54,47,55,62,63]
# inverse zigzag: position in raster order -> zigzag index
IZIG=[0]*64
for i,z in enumerate(ZIG): IZIG[z]=i

def build_huff(bits, vals):
    # returns dict symbol -> (code, length)
    code=0; k=0; out={}
    for l in range(1,17):
        for _ in range(bits[l-1]):
            out[vals[k]]=(code,l); code+=1; k+=1
        code <<= 1
    return out

def mk_table(tcid, tc, bits, vals):
    d = bytearray()
    d.append((tc<<4)|tcid)
    d += bytes(bits)
    d += bytes(vals)
    return d

def gen_tables():
    # AC: 256 symbols, 8 bits each
    bits=[0]*16; bits[7]=256
    vals=list(range(256))
    ac=mk_table(0,1,bits,vals)
    # DC: 16 symbols, 4 bits each
    bits=[0]*16; bits[3]=16
    vals=list(range(16))
    dc=mk_table(0,0,bits,vals)
    return [dc,ac]

DHT = gen_tables()

def fdct8x8(blk):
    # blk: list of 64 floats, raster order. returns 64 floats raster order
    import math
    C=[math.cos((2*i+1)*k*math.pi/16.0)/2.0 for i in range(8) for k in range(8)]
    # forward DCT: F(u,v) = 1/4 C(u) C(v) sum f(y,x) cos((2x+1)u pi/16) cos((2y+1) v pi/16)
    # where C(0)=1/sqrt2
    s=[0.5/2.0 if i else 0.0 for i in range(8)]
    # coefficients c_u = (u==0?1/sqrt2:1)/2
    def cu(u): return (1.0/math.sqrt(2.0) if u==0 else 1.0)/2.0
    out=[0.0]*64
    # separable: first rows then cols
    tmp=[0.0]*64
    for y in range(8):
        for u in range(8):
            t=0.0
            for x in range(8):
                t+= blk[y*8+x]*C[x*8+u]
            tmp[y*8+u]=t
    for u in range(8):
        for v in range(8):
            t=0.0
            for y in range(8):
                t+= tmp[y*8+u]*C[y*8+v]
            out[v*8+u]=t
    return out

    co = fdct8x8(blk)
    zz=[0]*64
    for i in range(64):
        v = co[IZIG[i]] / qt[IZIG[i]]   # careful: zigzag mapping
        zz[i] = int(round(v))
    bits=[]
    dc = zz[0]-prevdc
    cat = 0
    a = abs(dc)
    while a:
        cat+=1; a>>=1
    c,l = htab_dc[cat]
    bits.append((c,l))
    if cat:
        if dc<0: dc = dc + (1<<cat)-1
        bits.append((dc & ((1<<cat)-1), cat))
    # AC
    run=0

    w=bsize*nvals; h=bsize*rows

    return px,w,h

import subprocess, os
os.environ['TERM']='xterm'
def run(f,sz):

    d=p.stderr.split(b'\r')
    out=[]
    for l in d:
        if b'Decompressing image [' in l:
            i=l.index(b'['); j=l.index(b']')
            out.append((l[i+1:j]).count(b'#'))
    return out, p.returncode
for H in [8,12,16,17,24,25,32,33,48,50,64]:
    f='/tmp/h%02d.jpe'%H
    n,rc=run(f,'8x2')
    print('H=%d n=%d'%(H,len(n)), n)
EOF"}

actions.command:
cd /workspace && python3 - <<'EOF'
import subprocess, os
os.environ['TERM']='xterm'
def run(f,sz):
    p=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','-v','--size='+sz,f], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    d=p.stderr.split(b'\r')
    out=[]
    for l in d:
        if b'Decompressing image [' in l:
            i=l.index(b'['); j=l.index(b']')
            out.append((l[i+1:j]).count(b'#'))
    return out, p.returncode
for H in [8,12,16,17,24,25,32,33,48,50,64]:
    f='/tmp/h%02d.jpe'%H
    n,rc=run(f,'8x2')
    print('H=%d n=%d'%(H,len(n)), n)
EOF

print([(p,a,b,ch) for p,a,b,ch in out])
EOF
}

def encode_ycrc(pixels, w, h, ycc, qtbl=None):
    """pixels: rows of [Y, Cb, Cr] triples (all components 1x1 sampled)"""
    if qtbl is None:
        qtbl=[[1]*64,[1]*64]
    out=bytearray(b'\xff\xd8')
    app0=bytearray(b'JFIF\x00\x01\x01\x00\x00\x01\x00\x01\x00\x00')
    out+=marker(0xE0, app0)
    for t in range(2):
        d=bytearray([t]); d+=bytes(qtbl[t])
        out+=marker(0xDB, d)
    sof=bytearray([8,(h>>8)&0xFF,h&0xFF,(w>>8)&0xFF,w&0xFF,3])
    for cid in (1,2,3):
        sof.append(cid); sof.append(0x11); sof.append(0 if cid==1 else 1)
    out+=marker(0xC0, sof)
    ht_out=bytearray()
    for d in DHT: ht_out+=d
    out+=marker(0xC4, ht_out)
    sos=bytearray([3])
    for cid in (1,2,3):
        sos.append(cid); sos.append(0x00 if cid==1 else 0x11)
    sos+=bytearray([0,63,0])
    out+=marker(0xDA, sos)
    bits=[0]*16; bits[3]=15; htab_dc=build_huff(bits, list(range(15)))
    bits=[0]*16; bits[7]=128; bits[8]=128; htab_ac=build_huff(bits, list(range(256)))
    bw=BitWriter()
    mc_h=(h+7)//8*8; mc_w=(w+7)//8*8
    def get(y,x):
        yy=min(y,h-1); xx=min(x,w-1)
        return pixels[yy][xx]
    prevdc=[0,0,0]
    for by in range(0,mc_h,8):
        for bx in range(0,mc_w,8):
            for ci in range(3):
                blk=[0.0]*64
                for y in range(8):
                    for x in range(8):
                        blk[y*8+x]=get(by+y,bx+x)[ci]-128.0
                b,dc=encode_block(blk, prevdc[ci], qtbl[0 if ci==0 else 1], htab_dc, htab_ac)
                prevdc[ci]=dc
                for c,l in b: bw.put(c,l)
    bw.flush()
    out+=bw.out
    out+=b'\xff\xd9'
    return bytes(out)

def rgb2ycc(r,g,b):
    y = 0.299*r+0.587*g+0.114*b
    cb = (b-y)*0.564 + 128
    cr = (r-y)*0.713 + 128
    return y, cb, cr
PYEOF

def encode_ycrc(pixels, w, h, ycc, qtbl=None):
    """pixels: rows of [Y, Cb, Cr] triples (all components 1x1 sampled)"""
    if qtbl is None:
        qtbl=[[1]*64,[1]*64]
    out=bytearray(b'\xff\xd8')
    app0=bytearray(b'JFIF\x00\x01\x01\x00\x00\x01\x00\x01\x00\x00')
    out+=marker(0xE0, app0)
    for t in range(2):
        d=bytearray([t]); d+=bytes(qtbl[t])
        out+=marker(0xDB, d)
    sof=bytearray([8,(h>>8)&0xFF,h&0xFF,(w>>8)&0xFF,w&0xFF,3])
    for cid in (1,2,3):
        sof.append(cid); sof.append(0x11); sof.append(0 if cid==1 else 1)
    out+=marker(0xC0, sof)
    ht_out=bytearray()
    for d in DHT: ht_out+=d
    out+=marker(0xC4, ht_out)
    sos=bytearray([3])
    for cid in (1,2,3):
        sos.append(cid); sos.append(0x00 if cid==1 else 0x11)
    sos+=bytearray([0,63,0])
    out+=marker(0xDA, sos)
    bits=[0]*16; bits[3]=15; htab_dc=build_huff(bits, list(range(15)))
    bits=[0]*16; bits[7]=128; bits[8]=128; htab_ac=build_huff(bits, list(range(256)))
    bw=BitWriter()
    mc_h=(h+7)//8*8; mc_w=(w+7)//8*8
    def get(y,x):
        yy=min(y,h-1); xx=min(x,w-1)
        return pixels[yy][xx]
    prevdc=[0,0,0]
    for by in range(0,mc_h,8):
        for bx in range(0,mc_w,8):
            for ci in range(3):
                blk=[0.0]*64
                for y in range(8):
                    for x in range(8):
                        blk[y*8+x]=get(by+y,bx+x)[ci]-128.0
                b,dc=encode_block(blk, prevdc[ci], qtbl[0 if ci==0 else 1], htab_dc, htab_ac)
                prevdc[ci]=dc
                for c,l in b: bw.put(c,l)
    bw.flush()
    out+=bw.out
    out+=b'\xff\xd9'
    return bytes(out)

def rgb2ycc(r,g,b):
    y = 0.299*r+0.587*g+0.114*b
    cb = (b-y)*0.564 + 128
    cr = (r-y)*0.713 + 128
    return y, cb, cr
PYEOF

Hmm! So w must have been 2048 when I called it. Let me check my test script: `open('/tmp/crramp.jpe','wb').write(jenc.encode_ycrc(px,w,h))` with w=bsize*N = 8*256 = 2048! Ah — N=256 and bsize=8 → w = 2048 ✓. I made a mistake: I wanted 64 blocks but used N=256. So the image is 2048 wide with 256 blocks, each 8 wide ✓, and cr = k for k=0..255 ✓.

So my targets are correct for k=0..255 and the output columns are 256 → scale = 2048/256 = 8 → column x → source column 8x → block x ✓.

Now the program's R and G as functions of cr:
R: 0 for cr ≤ 82, then increasing to 255 at cr=191, then 255.
Actually from the dump: R=0 until x=82 (x=82 → 0), x=83 → 2. And R=255 from x=174 onwards (x=173 → 254, x=174 → 255).

Actually, hold on! Maybe the issue is my *encoder*: in encode_block I compute `co = fdct8x8(blk)` where blk contains (v-128). Hmm, so my encoding is fine for the DC. But my `fdct8x8` implementation: let me check the C array. So for a constant block of value c: out[0][0] = (1/4)*(1/2)*64*c = 8c ✓.

So the DC coefficient = 8*(v-128) ✓, and quantized with table all-1s → 8*(v-128) ✓.

Hmm, so the encoder should be fine. Let me verify by encoding a *grayscale* image with a known ramp and checking the output — I did that (ramp256) and the mapping matched my expectations ✓. So grayscale is fine.

So why would the chroma be doubled? 

OH!!! I bet I know: the *quantization tables*. I used table 0 for Y and table 1 for chroma — but in my encode_ycrc, I passed qtbl[0 if ci==0 else 1] ✓ and both are all-1s.

Hmm. What about the DHT tables: I provided dc0, ac0, dc1, ac1 ✓.

Hmm, so what's different about the chroma? Let me test: create a color image where only Cb varies (cr=128) and see the B values. If B = 128 + 1.772*2*(cb-128), then it's a 2x factor on chroma.

Actually, hold on. Let me reconsider: maybe the program's Y is NOT 128 but varies with cr! Let's check: if Y = 128 + s*(cr-128), then R = Y + 1.402*(cr-128)*... hmm.

Let's use the data: R(cr) and G(cr) and B(cr)=128. From R = Y + 1.402*(Cr-128) and G = Y - 0.714*(Cr-128) (with Cb=128, ignoring the +1 bias):
R - G = (1.402+0.714)*(cr-128) = 2.116*(cr-128). Observed: R-G at cr=128 = 0 ✓; at cr=173: 254-64 = 190; 2.116*45 = 95.2 ✗. Hmm.

Observed R-G: at cr=83: 2-192 = -190; at cr=173: 254-64 = 190. So (R-G)/2 = 95 over 45 units → slope 2.116 ✓!! So R-G = 2.116*(cr-128) — consistent with R = Y + 1.402*(cr-128), G = Y - 0.714*(cr-128) ✓ (in terms of the *difference*).

So the difference R-G follows the standard formula, but both R and G are shifted by the same amount. R+G = 2Y + (1.402-0.714)*(cr-128) = 2Y + 0.688*(cr-128). Observed R+G at cr=83: 194; at cr=173: 318. Slope = (318-194)/90 = 1.378 ≈ 0.688*2 = 1.376 ✓ (2x again!).

So the R+G slope is 2x the expected. So either Y varies with 2x the expected dependence on cr (i.e., Y depends on Cr with slope 0.688), or the Cr input is doubled.

If Cr_input = 2*(cr-128)+128 = 2cr-128, then R = Y + 1.402*(2cr-256) = Y + 2.804*(cr-128) and G = Y - 1.428*(cr-128) → R-G = 4.232*(cr-128). Observed 2.116. ✗ (that's 2x too much).

Hmm. So: R-G slope 2.116 (standard), R+G slope 1.376 (2x standard). That means Y varies with cr with slope 0.688 = (1.376 - 0)/2... let me solve:
R = Y(cr) + 1.402*(cr-128) → slope_R = slope_Y + 1.402 = 2.8 → slope_Y = 1.398
G = Y(cr) - 0.714*(cr-128) → slope_G = slope_Y - 0.714 = -1.4219 → slope_Y = -0.708
Contradiction! So the slopes don't fit a single Y function with the standard coefficients.

Hmm. So maybe the coefficients are different. Let's solve for a general linear model:
R = a0 + a1*cr, G = b0 + b1*cr, B = c0 + c1*cr (with Cb=128, Y=128).
Observed slopes: a1 = 2.8, b1 = -1.4219, c1 = 0.

Standard: a1 = 1.402, b1 = -0.714, c1 = 0. So the observed slopes are 2x the standard for R and G!

So the chroma contributions are DOUBLED. Interesting!

Hmm, why? 2x... 

OH!!! I think I've got it: maybe the program is reading the image with libjpeg in a mode where the chroma is... hmm.

Hmm, what if libjpeg's JFIF/Adobe handling assumes the component order is Y,Cb,Cr ✓ (that's standard).

Hmm, so why 2x?

Hmm, what if the *quantization* of the chroma DC is different: if the chroma quant table value were 0.5, the DC would be doubled... but quant table values must be ≥ 1.

Actually, hold on. Let me reconsider the possibility that the program's Y is not constant but *varies* with cr in a way that produces the observed values. We showed that's impossible with a single Y. Unless the program's luminance for the *character* mapping differs from the color...

cd /tmp && python3 - <<'EOF'
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/tools'); import jenc
for vals in [[0,255],[255,0],[0,0],[255,255],[0,128],[0,64],[64,192],[0,255,0,255]]:
    w=8*len(vals); h=8
    px=[[[(v)] for v in vals for _ in range(8)] for y in range(h)]
    open('/tmp/t2.jpe','wb').write(jenc.encode(px,w,h,1))
    print(vals, end=' -> ')
    import subprocess,os
    os.environ['TERM']='xterm'
    r=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','--html','--colors','--html-raw','--size=%dx1'%(len(vals)),'/tmp/t2.jpe'],capture_output=True)
    import re
    cols=re.findall(r"color:#([0-9a-f]{6});'", r.stdout.decode())
    print(cols)
EOF

cd /workspace && export TERM=xterm
cd /tmp && python3 -c "
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/tools'); import jenc

actions.command:
cd /workspace && export TERM=xterm
for pair in "100,101" "127,128" "128,129" "129,130" "50,51" "200,201" "128,128" "129,129"; do
 cd /tmp && python3 -c "
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/tools'); import jenc
vals=[$pair]
w=16; h=8
px=[[[(v)] for v in vals for _ in range(8)] for y in range(h)]
open('/tmp/tr.jpe','wb').write(jenc.encode(px,w,h,1))
"
 cd /workspace && printf "%s: " "$pair"; ./executable --html --colors --html-raw --size=16x1 /tmp/tr.jpe | grep -o "color:#[0-9a-f]*" | sed 's/color:#//' | tr '\n' ' '; echo
done
echo "=== 4 blocks:"
for pair in "128,129,128,129" "100,101,100,101"; do
 cd /tmp && python3 -c "
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/tools'); import jenc
vals=[$pair]
w=32; h=8
px=[[[(v)] for v in vals for _ in range(8)] for y in range(h)]
open('/tmp/tr4.jpe','wb').write(jenc.encode(px,w,h,1))
"
 cd /workspace && printf "%s: " "$pair"; ./executable --html --colors --html-raw --size=32x1 /tmp/tr4.jpe | grep -o "color:#[0-9a-f]*" | sed 's/color:#//' | tr '\n' ' '; echo
done

"""Full baseline JPEG decoder (validates my encoder)."""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/tools')
from jdec import parse, Bits, build, decode_sym, ZIG, IZIG
import math

def idct8x8(coef):
    """coef: 64 floats raster order, returns 64 floats raster order (level-shifted back by caller)"""
    C=[math.cos((2*i+1)*k*math.pi/16.0)/2.0*(1.0/math.sqrt(2.0) if k==0 else 1.0) for i in range(8) for k in range(8)]
    tmp=[0.0]*64
    for v in range(8):
        for x in range(8):
            t=0.0
            for u in range(8):
                t+=coef[v*8+u]*C[x*8+u]
            tmp[v*8+x]=t
    out=[0.0]*64
    for y in range(8):
        for x in range(8):
            t=0.0
            for v in range(8):
                t+=tmp[v*8+x]*C[y*8+v]
            out[y*8+x]=t
    return out

def decode_blocks(data):
    qt,ht,sof,sos,entropy=parse(data)
    prec,h,w,comps=sof
    sels,ss,se,ahal=sos
    br=Bits(entropy)
    nc=len(comps)
    bw=(w+7)//8; bh=(h+7)//8
    maxh=max(c[1] for c in comps); maxv=max(c[2] for c in comps)
    mcux=(bw+maxh-1)//maxh; mcuy=(bh+maxv-1)//maxv
    planes=[[[0]*w for y in range(h)] for _ in range(nc)]
    prev=[0]*nc
    for my in range(mcuy):
        for mx in range(mcux):
            for ci,comp in enumerate(comps):
                cid,hv,vv,tq=comp
                td,ta=sels[ci][1],sels[ci][2]
                dct=ht[(0,td)]; act=ht[(1,ta)]
                cat=decode_sym(br,dct)
                diff=0
                if cat:
                    v=br.bits(cat)
                    if v < (1<<(cat-1)): v -= (1<<cat)-1
                    diff=v
                prev[ci]+=diff
                zz=[0]*64
                zz[0]=prev[ci]
                k=1
                while k<64:
                    rs=decode_sym(br,act)
                    if rs==0: break
                    run=rs>>4; size=rs&15
                    if size==0:
                        if run==15: k+=16; continue
                        else: break
                    k+=run
                    v=br.bits(size)
                    if v < (1<<(size-1)): v -= (1<<size)-1
                    if k<64:
                        zz[IZIG[k]]=v*qt[tq][IZIG[k]]
                    k+=1
                coef=[0.0]*64
                for i in range(64): coef[i]=zz[i]*qt[tq][i]
                px=idct8x8(coef)
                # place
                bh0=my*maxv*8 + 0; bw0=mx*maxh*8
                for yy in range(8):
                    for xx in range(8):
                        y=my*maxv*8+yy; x=mx*maxh*8+xx
                        if y<h and x<w:
                            planes[ci][y][x]=max(0,min(255,int(round(px[yy*8+x]+128))))
    return sof, planes

if __name__=='__main__':
    data=open(sys.argv[1],'rb').read()
    sof,planes=decode_blocks(data)
    print('sof',sof)
    print('row0', planes[0][0])

from jdec import parse, Bits, build, decode_sym, ZIG, IZIG
import math

def idct8x8(coef):

    C=[math.cos((2*i+1)*k*math.pi/16.0)/2.0*(1.0/math.sqrt(2.0) if k==0 else 1.0) for i in range(8) for k in range(8)]

            t=0.0
            for u in range(8):

            tmp[v*8+x]=t

    for y in range(8):
        for x in range(8):
            t=0.0
            for v in range(8):
                t+=tmp[v*8+x]*C[y*8+v]
            out[y*8+x]=t
    return out

from jdec import parse, Bits, decode_sym, ZIG, IZIG

def idct8x8(coef):

    C=[math.cos((2*i+1)*k*math.pi/16.0)/2.0*(1.0/math.sqrt(2.0) if k==0 else 1.0) for i in range(8) for k in range(8)]
    tmp=[0.0]*64
    for v in range(8):
        for x in range(8):
            tmp[v*8+x]=sum(coef[v*8+u]*C[x*8+u] for u in range(8))
    out=[0.0]*64
    for y in range(8):
        for x in range(8):
            out[y*8+x]=sum(tmp[v*8+x]*C[y*8+v] for v in range(8))
    return out

import jenc
from jdec import parse, Bits, decode_sym, IZIG, build, stdhuff if False else None
import jdec
def idct8x8(coef):
    C=[math.cos((2*i+1)*k*math.pi/16.0)/2.0*(1.0/math.sqrt(2.0) if k==0 else 1.0) for i in range(8) for k in range(8)]

            tmp[v*8+x]=sum(coef[v*8+u]*C[x*8+u] for u in range(8))

    for y in range(8):
        for x in range(8):
            out[y*8+x]=sum(tmp[v*8+x]*C[y*8+v] for v in range(8))
    return out
data=open('/tmp/sin2.jpe','rb').read()
qt,ht,sof,sos,entropy=jdec.parse(data)

bits=''.join(format(b,'08b') for b in entropy)

br=Bits(entropy)
dct=ht[(0,0)]; act=ht[(1,0)]
prev=0
for blk in range(1):
    cat=decode_sym(br,dct)
    diff=0
    if cat:
        v=br.bits(cat)
        if v<(1<<(cat-1)): v-=(1<<cat)-1
        diff=v
    prev+=diff
    zz=[0]*64; zz[0]=prev
    k=1
    while k<64:
        rs=decode_sym(br,act)
        if rs==0: break
        run=rs>>4; size=rs&15
        if size==0:
            if run==15: k+=16; continue
            break
        k+=run
        v=br.bits(size)
        if v<(1<<(size-1)): v-=(1<<size)-1

cd /tmp && python3 - <<'EOF'
import sys, math; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/tools'); import jenc
import stdhuff
# monkeypatch encode_block to dump zz and the emitted symbols
orig=jenc.encode_block
def enc(blk, prevdc, qt, hd, ha):
    co=jenc.fdct8x8(blk)
    zz=[int(round(co[jenc.IZIG[i]]/qt[jenc.IZIG[i]])) for i in range(64)]
    print('zz nonzero:', [(i,zz[i]) for i in range(64) if zz[i]])
    b,dc=orig(blk,prevdc,qt,hd,ha)
    print('emitted:', b)
    return b,dc
jenc.encode_block=enc
w=8; h=8
px=[[[(round(128+100*math.cos((2*x+1)*2*math.pi/16.0)))] for x in range(w)] for y in range(h)]
data=jenc.encode(px,w,h,1,huff='std')
EOF

import sys, math; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/tools')
import jdec
from jdec import parse, Bits, decode_sym, ZIG
def idct8x8(coef):
    C=[math.cos((2*i+1)*k*math.pi/16.0)/2.0*(1.0/math.sqrt(2.0) if k==0 else 1.0) for i in range(8) for k in range(8)]
    tmp=[0.0]*64
    for v in range(8):
        for x in range(8):
            tmp[v*8+x]=sum(coef[v*8+u]*C[x*8+u] for u in range(8))
    out=[0.0]*64
    for y in range(8):
        for x in range(8):
            out[y*8+x]=sum(tmp[v*8+x]*C[y*8+v] for v in range(8))
    return out
for fn in ['/tmp/sin1.jpe','/tmp/sin2.jpe','/tmp/kk04.jpe']:
    data=open(fn,'rb').read()
    qt,ht,sof,sos,entropy=jdec.parse(data)
    br=Bits(entropy)
    prev=0
    coef=[0.0]*64
    cat=decode_sym(br,ht[(0,0)])
    diff=0
    if cat:
        v=br.bits(cat)
        if v<(1<<(cat-1)): v-=(1<<cat)-1
        diff=v
    prev+=diff
    zz=[0]*64; zz[0]=prev
    k=1
    while k<64:
        rs=decode_sym(br,ht[(1,0)])
        if rs==0: break
        run=rs>>4; size=rs&15
        if size==0:
            if run==15: k+=16; continue
            break
        k+=run
        v=br.bits(size)
        if v<(1<<(size-1)): v-=(1<<size)-1
        if k<64: zz[k]=v
        k+=1
    for i in range(64): coef[i]=zz[i]*qt[0][i]
    # place: zz[i] is zigzag i -> raster ZIG[i]
    raster=[0.0]*64
    for i in range(64): raster[ZIG[i]]=coef[i]
    px=idct8x8(raster)
    print(fn, 'row0:', [round(p+128) for p in px[:8]])
EOF

cd /tmp && python3 - <<'EOF'
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/tools'); import jenc
# color ramp: Y=128, Cb=128, Cr=k  (k=0..255)
N=256; bsize=8
w=bsize*N; h=bsize
px=[[ [128.0,128.0,float(x//bsize)] for x in range(w)] for y in range(h)]
open('/tmp/crramp.jpe','wb').write(jenc.encode_ycrc(px,w,h,huff='std'))
# Cb ramp
px=[[ [128.0,float(x//bsize),128.0] for x in range(w)] for y in range(h)]
open('/tmp/cbramp.jpe','wb').write(jenc.encode_ycrc(px,w,h,huff='std'))
# Y ramp (3 comp)
px=[[ [float(x//bsize),128.0,128.0] for x in range(w)] for y in range(h)]
open('/tmp/yramp.jpe','wb').write(jenc.encode_ycrc(px,w,h,huff='std'))
# grid
pts=[]
for Y in [0,32,64,96,128,160,192,224,255]:
    for CB in [0,64,128,192,255]:
        for CR in [0,64,128,192,255]:
            pts.append((Y,CB,CR))
w2=8*len(pts); h2=8
row=[]
for k in range(len(pts)):
    a,b,c=pts[k]
    for _ in range(8): row.append([float(a),float(b),float(c)])
px2=[list(row) for _ in range(h2)]
open('/tmp/grid.jpe','wb').write(jenc.encode_ycrc(px2,w2,h2,huff='std'))
import json; json.dump(pts, open('/tmp/pts.json','w'))
print('ok')
EOF
cd /workspace && export TERM=xterm
echo "=== Y ramp (3comp, Cb=Cr=128) colors:"; ./executable --html --colors --html-raw --size=256x1 /tmp/yramp.jpe | grep -o "color:#[0-9a-f]*" | sed 's/color:#//' | tr '\n' ' ' | head -c 600; echo
echo "=== chars:"; ./executable --size=256x1 /tmp/yramp.jpe

import sys, math
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/tools')
from jdec import parse, Bits, decode_sym, ZIG
import ycc
def idct8x8(coef):
    C=[math.cos((2*i+1)*k*math.pi/16.0)/2.0*(1.0/math.sqrt(2.0) if k==0 else 1.0) for i in range(8) for k in range(8)]
    tmp=[0.0]*64
    for v in range(8):
        for x in range(8):
            tmp[v*8+x]=sum(coef[v*8+u]*C[x*8+u] for u in range(8))
    out=[0.0]*64
    for y in range(8):
        for x in range(8):
            out[y*8+x]=sum(tmp[v*8+x]*C[y*8+v] for v in range(8))
    return out

def decode(fn, maxrows=None):
    data=open(fn,'rb').read()
    qt,ht,sof,sos,entropy=parse(data)
    prec,h,w,comps=sof
    sels,ss,se,ahal=sos
    nc=len(comps)
    if maxrows: h=min(h,maxrows)
    br=Bits(entropy)
    planes=[[[0]*w for y in range(h)] for _ in range(nc)]
    prev=[0]*nc
    bw=(w+7)//8; bh=(h+7)//8
    maxh=max(c[1] for c in comps); maxv=max(c[2] for c in comps)
    mcux=(bw+maxh-1)//maxh; mcuy=(bh+maxv-1)//maxv
    # block positions per component
    nbx=[(bw+c[1]-1)//c[1] for c in comps]
    nby=[(bh+c[2]-1)//c[2] for c in comps]
    for my in range(mcuy):
        for mx in range(mcux):
            for ci,comp in enumerate(comps):
                cid,hv,vv,tq=comp
                td,ta=sels[ci][1],sels[ci][2]
                dct=ht[(0,td)]; act=ht[(1,ta)]
                cat=decode_sym(br,dct)
                diff=0
                if cat:
                    v=br.bits(cat)
                    if v < (1<<(cat-1)): v -= (1<<cat)-1
                    diff=v
                prev[ci]+=diff
                zz=[0]*64; zz[0]=prev[ci]
                k=1
                while k<64:
                    rs=decode_sym(br,act)
                    if rs==0: break
                    run=rs>>4; size=rs&15
                    if size==0:
                        if run==15: k+=16; continue
                        break
                    k+=run
                    v=br.bits(size)
                    if v < (1<<(size-1)): v -= (1<<size)-1
                    if k<64: zz[k]=v
                    k+=1
                # dequantize & place
                for yb in range(vv):
                    for xb in range(hv):
                        by=my*maxv+yb; bx=mx*maxh+xb
                        if by>=nby[ci] or bx>=nbx[ci]: continue
                        coef=[0.0]*64
                        for i in range(64):
                            coef[i]=zz[i]*qt[tq][i]
                        raster=[0.0]*64
                        for i in range(64): raster[ZIG[i]]=coef[i]
                        px=idct8x8(raster)
                        for yy in range(8):
                            for xx in range(8):

                                if y<h and x<w:
                                    planes[ci][y][x]=max(0,min(255,int(round(px[yy*8+x]+128))))
    return sof, planes

import sys, math
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/tools')
from jdec import parse, Bits, decode_sym, ZIG
import ycc
def idct8x8(coef):
    C=[math.cos((2*i+1)*k*math.pi/16.0)/2.0*(1.0/math.sqrt(2.0) if k==0 else 1.0) for i in range(8) for k in range(8)]
    tmp=[0.0]*64
    for v in range(8):
        for x in range(8):
            tmp[v*8+x]=sum(coef[v*8+u]*C[x*8+u] for u in range(8))
    out=[0.0]*64
    for y in range(8):
        for x in range(8):
            out[y*8+x]=sum(tmp[v*8+x]*C[y*8+v] for v in range(8))
    return out

def decode(fn, maxrows=None):
    data=open(fn,'rb').read()
    qt,ht,sof,sos,entropy=parse(data)
    prec,h,w,comps=sof
    sels,ss,se,ahal=sos
    nc=len(comps)
    if maxrows: h=min(h,maxrows)
    br=Bits(entropy)
    planes=[[[0]*w for y in range(h)] for _ in range(nc)]
    prev=[0]*nc
    bw=(w+7)//8; bh=(h+7)//8
    maxh=max(c[1] for c in comps); maxv=max(c[2] for c in comps)
    mcux=(bw+maxh-1)//maxh; mcuy=(bh+maxv-1)//maxv
    # block positions per component
    nbx=[(bw+c[1]-1)//c[1] for c in comps]
    nby=[(bh+c[2]-1)//c[2] for c in comps]
    for my in range(mcuy):
        for mx in range(mcux):
            for ci,comp in enumerate(comps):
                cid,hv,vv,tq=comp
                td,ta=sels[ci][1],sels[ci][2]
                dct=ht[(0,td)]; act=ht[(1,ta)]
                cat=decode_sym(br,dct)
                diff=0
                if cat:
                    v=br.bits(cat)
                    if v < (1<<(cat-1)): v -= (1<<cat)-1
                    diff=v
                prev[ci]+=diff
                zz=[0]*64; zz[0]=prev[ci]
                k=1
                while k<64:
                    rs=decode_sym(br,act)
                    if rs==0: break
                    run=rs>>4; size=rs&15
                    if size==0:
                        if run==15: k+=16; continue
                        break
                    k+=run
                    v=br.bits(size)
                    if v < (1<<(size-1)): v -= (1<<size)-1
                    if k<64: zz[k]=v
                    k+=1
                # dequantize & place
                for yb in range(vv):
                    for xb in range(hv):
                        by=my*maxv+yb; bx=mx*maxh+xb
                        if by>=nby[ci] or bx>=nbx[ci]: continue
                        coef=[0.0]*64
                        for i in range(64):

                        raster=[0.0]*64
                        for i in range(64): raster[ZIG[i]]=coef[i]

                        for yy in range(8):
                            for xx in range(8):

                                if y<h and x<w:
                                    planes[ci][y][x]=max(0,min(255,int(round(px[yy*8+x]+128))))
    return sof, planes

# check entropy decode: count bits consumed
class B:
    def __init__(s,d): s.d=d; s.pos=0; s.acc=0; s.n=0; s.marker=None; s.count=0
    def fill(s):
        while s.n<25:
            if s.pos>=len(s.d): break
            b=s.d[s.pos]; s.pos+=1
            if b==0xFF:
                nb=s.d[s.pos] if s.pos<len(s.d) else 0xD9
                if nb==0x00: s.pos+=1
                else:
                    s.marker=nb; s.n+=8; s.acc=(s.acc<<8)|0; continue
            s.acc=(s.acc<<8)|b; s.n+=8
    def bit(s):
        if s.n==0: s.fill()
        if s.n==0: raise EOFError
        s.n-=1; s.count+=1
        return (s.acc>>s.n)&1
    def bits(s,k):
        v=0
        for _ in range(k): v=(v<<1)|s.bit()

"""Generate baseline JPEG files from raw coefficient blocks (1 component, 8x8 blocks)."""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/tools')
import jenc
ZIG=jenc.ZIG
IZIG=jenc.IZIG

def build(coeffs_blocks, w, h, qt=None, huff='std'):
    """coeffs_blocks: list of blocks (row-major list of blocks), each block = list of 64 values in ZIGZAG order."""
    if qt is None: qt=[1]*64
    out=bytearray(b'\xff\xd8')
    out+=jenc.marker(0xE0, bytearray(b'JFIF\x00\x01\x01\x00\x00\x01\x00\x01\x00\x00'))
    d=bytearray([0]); d+=bytes(qt)
    out+=jenc.marker(0xDB, d)
    sof=bytearray([8,(h>>8)&0xFF,h&0xFF,(w>>8)&0xFF,w&0xFF,1])
    sof+=bytes([1,0x11,0])
    out+=jenc.marker(0xC0, sof)
    dht=bytearray()
    import stdhuff
    for t in jenc.STD_DHT: dht+=t
    out+=jenc.marker(0xC4, dht)
    sos=bytearray([1, 1, 0x00]); sos+=bytearray([0,63,0])
    out+=jenc.marker(0xDA, sos)
    htab_dc=jenc.build_huff(stdhuff.STD_DC_LUM_BITS, stdhuff.STD_DC_LUM_VALS)
    htab_ac=jenc.build_huff(stdhuff.STD_AC_LUM_BITS, stdhuff.STD_AC_LUM_VALS)
    bw=jenc.BitWriter()
    prev=0
    for blk in coeffs_blocks:
        zz=list(blk)
        bits=[]
        dc=zz[0]-prev; prev=zz[0]
        cat=0; a=abs(dc)
        while a: cat+=1; a>>=1
        c,l=htab_dc[cat]; bits.append((c,l))
        if cat:
            v=dc if dc>0 else dc+((1<<cat)-1)
            bits.append((v & ((1<<cat)-1), cat))
        run=0
        for i in range(1,64):
            v=zz[i]
            if v==0: run+=1; continue
            while run>15:
                c,l=htab_ac[0xF0]; bits.append((c,l)); run-=16
            cat=0; a=abs(v)
            while a: cat+=1; a>>=1
            s=run*16+cat
            c,l=htab_ac[s]; bits.append((c,l))
            ev=v if v>0 else v+((1<<cat)-1)
            bits.append((ev & ((1<<cat)-1), cat))
            run=0
        if run>0:
            c,l=htab_ac[0]; bits.append((c,l))
        for c,l in bits: bw.put(c,l)
    bw.flush()
    out+=bw.out
    out+=b'\xff\xd9'
    return bytes(out)
PYEOF

import sys

def build(coeffs_blocks, w, h, qt=None, huff='std'):
    """coeffs_blocks: list of blocks (row-major list of blocks), each block = list of 64 values in ZIGZAG order."""
    if qt is None: qt=[1]*64

    out+=jenc.marker(0xDB, d)
    sof=bytearray([8,(h>>8)&0xFF,h&0xFF,(w>>8)&0xFF,w&0xFF,1])
    sof+=bytes([1,0x11,0])
    out+=jenc.marker(0xC0, sof)
    dht=bytearray()
    import stdhuff
    for t in jenc.STD_DHT: dht+=t
    out+=jenc.marker(0xC4, dht)
    sos=bytearray([1, 1, 0x00]); sos+=bytearray([0,63,0])
    out+=jenc.marker(0xDA, sos)

        dc=zz[0]-prev; prev=zz[0]
        cat=0; a=abs(dc)
        while a: cat+=1; a>>=1
        c,l=htab_dc[cat]; bits.append((c,l))
        if cat:

        run=0
        for i in range(1,64):

            while run>15:
                c,l=htab_ac[0xF0]; bits.append((c,l)); run-=16
            cat=0; a=abs(v)
            while a: cat+=1; a>>=1
            s=run*16+cat
            c,l=htab_ac[s]; bits.append((c,l))
            ev=v if v>0 else v+((1<<cat)-1)
            bits.append((ev & ((1<<cat)-1), cat))
            run=0
        if run>0:
            c,l=htab_ac[0]; bits.append((c,l))

PYEOF
